key_insight: Phase-engineered bismuth-based oxide double-perovskites BFCO and BMCO can absorb visible light strongly and operate as lead-free photovoltaic absorbers, with BMCO demonstrating a first-device power conversion efficiency of 3.56%.
engineering_relevance: These materials offer a safer, potentially more stable alternative to lead halide perovskites, with band-edge information that can guide charge-transport-layer selection and device stack design.
method: Solution-deposited BFCO and BMCO thin films (350–450 nm) were synthesized and structurally verified as monoclinic P21/c double perovskites.
Optoelectronic characterization included visible-range absorption, carrier density estimation, and ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy for band-edge alignment.
A BMCO solar cell was fabricated in an FTO/SnO2/BMCO/Spiro-OMeTAD/Ag architecture and evaluated experimentally; numerical simulation assessed defect-limited performance potential.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong visible absorption (α ~ 10^4–10^5 cm^-1), high carrier density (~10^17–10^20 cm^-3), and a measured peak efficiency of 3.56% for the BMCO device.
watch_item: Performance is limited by mixed cation valences and deep-level defects, so defect control and interface optimization are critical before practical deployment.
paper_title: Beyond lead halide perovskites: visible light photovoltaics with phase engineered bismuth-based oxide double-perovskites, Bi2MCrO6 (M = Fe, Mn)
